nodes.label: Power of Mortgagor to Grant Permanent Lease
nodes.description: Whether prior to the enactment of section 65-A of the Transfer of Property Act in 1929, a mortgagor in possession had the power to grant a permanent lease of the mortgaged property so as to bind the mortgagee.

source_refs.exact_quote: J. and Chatterji J.) in Appeal from Original Decree No. 4 of 1941, arising out of Judgment and Decree dated the 20th September, 1940, of the Court of the Additional Subordinate Judge of Hazaribagh in Title Suit No. 45 of 1939. [IKWEB-1251841:L120] S. N. Mukherjee for the appellant. [IKWEB-1251841:L121] Gangacharan Mukherjee and A. N. Sinha for the respondents. 1952. October 23. The judgment of the Court was delivered by BHAGWATI J, 110 BHAGWATI J.-The question that arises for our consideration in this appeal is whether prior to the enactment of cite13†section 65-A of the Transfer of Property Act in 1929 a mortgagor in possession had the power to grant a permanent lease of the mortgaged property so as to bind the mortgagee.

nodes.label: Mortgagor Had No Power to Grant Permanent Lease
nodes.description: The Court held that Wazir Narayan Singh had no power to grant the permanent lease in question to the defendants, as it was not in the usual course of management.

source_refs.exact_quote: [IKWEB-1251841:L199] We have therefore come to the conclusion that Wazir Narayan Singh had no power to grant the permanent lease in question to the defendants, that the same was not binding and operative against the plaintiff, that the defendants had ample opportunity to@ redeem the mortgage if they so desired but did not choose to exercise their right of redemption, that the execution sale of Gadi Sirampur including the four villages in question was binding them and that the plaintiff was entitled to khas possession of the four villages of which the defendants were in wrongful possession.

nodes.label: Plaintiff Entitled to Khas Possession
nodes.description: The Court held that the plaintiff was entitled to khas possession of the four villages of which the defendants were in wrongful possession.

source_refs.exact_quote: [IKWEB-1251841:L199] We have therefore come to the conclusion that Wazir Narayan Singh had no power to grant the permanent lease in question to the defendants, that the same was not binding and operative against the plaintiff, that the defendants had ample opportunity to@ redeem the mortgage if they so desired but did not choose to exercise their right of redemption, that the execution sale of Gadi Sirampur including the four villages in question was binding them and that the plaintiff was entitled to khas possession of the four villages of which the defendants were in wrongful possession.
